speaker_role: student (high school senior admitted to Dartmouth and Stanford, vlogging her own experience)
key_insights: Student applied test-optional to Dartmouth (and all her schools) and did not submit SAT/ACT scores despite having scores (reports low ACT and mid-range SAT results), choosing to rely on other parts of the application instead.
She had strong grades overall (mostly A's/A+'s, one C in 9th grade in a rigorous class) and used her personal statement to explain the one low grade.

She emphasizes heavy, sustained extracurricular involvement across high school (choir/chair leadership, speech and debate, founding student government, journalism, multi-year internships) rather than one-off activities.

Her personal statement topic shifted from an early interest in medicine to arts/communications after realizing medicine wasn't her passion, and she argues that pivoting to what you're actually passionate about (rather than forcing a 'consistent' narrative) helped her essay feel genuine.

For Dartmouth's supplemental essay, she chose a prompt (a Frida Kahlo quote) and connected it to personal identity themes (being an immigrant, evolving views on gender roles) rather than writing generically about the school.
Advises writing about what genuinely resonates with you personally rather than what you think admissions wants to hear, arguing authenticity reads through to readers.

Notes that college outcomes can be inconsistent for similar-looking applicants because schools may be seeking specific types of students for their incoming class in a given year, so rejection shouldn't be taken personally.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Student reports an ACT score around 18 (taken twice, same result) and an SAT score she recalls as either 1080 or 1110.
Student applied to Columbia, UPenn, NYU, Stanford, and Dartmouth; was rejected from Columbia, UPenn, and NYU, and admitted to Dartmouth and Stanford.
notable_or_distinctive: A specific real (self-reported) data point of being admitted to Dartmouth and Stanford test-optional with a below-average ACT/SAT, illustrating how strong grades, sustained extracurriculars, and a personal essay can outweigh modest test scores in a test-optional context.
reliability_notes: Single anecdotal student account (survivorship bias — one admit doesn't establish what generally works), delivered in an unstructured, rambling vlog style typical of auto-captioned content; scores and details are self-reported and unverified, and 'why I got in' reasoning is speculative since she states she doesn't actually know why she was admitted.
